finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can inject a filename that includes shell metacharacters or control operators.
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate the 'filename' input before using it to open a file. The operating system may execute unintended commands if the filename includes shell metacharacters.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
Checked the sink operation at line 18: `ifstream infile(filename);`. This opens a file with the given path but does not invoke a shell or command interpreter. No system(), exec(), or similar call is present in the visible code, and the input is not passed to any external process. Therefore the claimed OS command injection is not applicable. The filename may be malformed or non‑existent, but it cannot cause shell command execution.

Evidence lines: 17 (input acquisition), 18 (file opening).

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: An attacker can inject a filename that includes shell metacharacters or control operators.
finding.assumptions: The code does not sanitize or validate the 'filename' input before using it to open a file. The operating system may execute unintended commands if the filename includes shell metacharacters.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any system or shell‑invoking functions; the only operation using the untrusted input is the construction of an ifstream object (line 18). In C++, ifstream::open simply opens a file at the specified path and does not invoke a shell or interpreter, so the input cannot be used to inject OS commands. The assumption that a filename with shell metacharacters could trigger command execution is incorrect.
